accuracy.evidence: Defines a minibeast as a small invertebrate, gives insects 6 legs and 3 body parts, spiders 8 legs and 2 parts, woodlice 14 legs as crustaceans, matching KS1 science guidance.

misconceptions.evidence: Adult text names small-means-minibeast (mouse), all-bugs-are-insects (spider, woodlouse), legless-means-not-an-animal (worm) and leaving logs turned over; the lab challenge why() answers each one.

lab_distinct.evidence: A bug-hunt lab: lift and replace log, stone and leaves, move a hand lens to count legs, sort by leg count; unlike the habitats lesson 390 or vertebrate groups lesson 508.

lab_teaches.evidence: Children discover the backbone rule with a mouse counterexample, then count legs under the lens themselves before the insect versus spider rule is stated in words.

predictions.evidence: Three predictions (is a mouse a minibeast, ladybird legs, is a spider an insect) are each checked by what the child then sees and counts in the lab, with spot-on or rethink feedback.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Seven challenge questions; each wrong option has its own why() reply, for example a robin has a backbone, or a worm with no legs is still an animal with no backbone.

readability.evidence: Kid paragraphs start with feeling your own backbone and use short concrete sentences; adult paragraphs list KS1 vocabulary such as invertebrate, hand lens and micro-habitat.

no_filler.evidence: Every paragraph defines the term, gives the leg counts, names a mistake or explains the lab; the family tip is a concrete ten-minute bug hunt with a hand lens.

mobile.evidence: iPhone 13 screenshots in light and dark show big young-mode buttons for lifting, lens and sorting, a readable lens view with 6 and 8 legs, and no horizontal overflow.

accessibility.evidence: Each drag action (lift, lens, sort) has a button twin; the canvas aria-label reports what was found and counted, and walk.cjs axe checks passed in both themes.

sources: UK National Curriculum 2013, Year 1 Science: Animals, including humans (identify and name common animals)
UK National Curriculum 2013, Year 2 Science: Living things and their habitats (micro-habitats, observe using simple equipment)
Natural History Museum / Field Studies Council guidance on invertebrate identification (insects 6 legs, arachnids 8, woodlice 14)
